svg.title: Why a tour cannot teach the two things a new user most needs
svg.desc: A tour highlights elements on screen, so its syllabus is limited to what a person could have found by looking: the sidebar, the new note button, the search field. The two facts that matter most on day one are not on screen — that a clipboard manager exists behind a keyboard shortcut outside the window, and that it can be switched off. A welcome can teach both, and can ask the user to press the shortcut once so the app can confirm it worked.
svg.text: A TOUR CAN ONLY POINT AT
All true, all visible, all discoverable by looking.
The format was choosing the syllabus.
outside the window, behind a shortcut
offered with the explanation, not buried later
“Press ⇧⌥V now” — and the app confirms it opened
A tour that teaches a shortcut which has deliberately not been registered is worse than one that
says nothing: the user tries it, nothing happens, and the false belief stays behind.
